What Is a Prompt?
An instruction, in plain English, that tells the AI what to produce
ANATOMY OF A PROMPT
“You are a B2B marketing strategist. Write three LinkedIn posts announcing our workshop for HR leaders in Pune, each under 80 words with one clear call to action.”
Role
Task
Context
Output format

The Building Process
Start small and simple, then gradually proceed
At every step: build → test → refine
STEP 1
Start small
One core feature that works
STEP 2
Make it work
Test with real inputs, fix what breaks
STEP 3
Add layers
One feature at a time
STEP 4
Scale up
Polish, automate, connect
STEP 1
Start small
One core feature that works
e.g. a simple sign-up form
STEP 2
Make it work
Test with real inputs, fix what breaks
e.g. validate emails, store leads
STEP 3
Add layers
One feature at a time
e.g. an automatic thank-you email
STEP 4
Scale up
Polish, automate, connect
e.g. a dashboard and CRM sync
Complexity grows one step at a time

Refining Claude's Output Without Burning Tokens
Better results with fewer, smarter prompts
01
Plan before you prompt
Design the app or workflow first, then write one clear brief
02
Front-load the context
Give everything upfront to avoid back-and-forth
03
Ask for targeted edits
“Change only section 3”, not “redo everything”
04
Batch your feedback
Combine all your changes into one message
05
Start fresh chats
Long threads resend their history each turn. New task, new chat
06
Reuse your instructions
Save briefs as .md files, skills or projects
